test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 20 Sept 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Which of the following explanations regarding the given reaction is correct?

Fe(s) + CuSO4(aq) → FeSO4(aq) + Cu(s)

options.text: Iron displaces copper because iron is more reactive than copper.
Iron displaces copper because iron is less reactive than copper.
Iron displaces copper because the atomic mass of iron is less than copper.
Iron displaces copper because the atomic number of iron is less than copper.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Iron displaces copper because iron is more reactive than copper.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** ****Fe is the reducing agent** in the given reaction and **CuSO4 is an oxidizing agent.**
 
• The given reaction is an **oxidation-reduction(redox) reaction**.
 
• **Displacement reaction**__
 __
 
• Displacement reactions occur when an atom or group of atoms in a molecule are** replaced by another atom ****​**__
 
• When one element in a compound is replaced by another, it causes a single displacement reaction.
 
• A metal only replaces a metal in a displacement reaction, while a non-metal only replaces a non-metal.
 
• **Less reactive components are replaced by more reactive ones.**
 
• We can infer from the reaction that when iron is introduced to a solution of copper sulphate, it displaces the copper metal and produces ferrous sulphate. It is a displacement response as a result.
